review_notes: Compared with skaudio.cpp::ALLOC_AUDIO_RAM_BUFFER at 44-56. Source initializes the IBMIO audio flag, checks for an installed sound card, allocates a 0x400-aligned source RAM sample buffer sized by glbMemRAMAudioStuff, zeroes/configures it, and enables buffered sound only for selected card types. Firestaff opens a 6000 Hz unsigned 8-bit SDL3 stream lazily on first playback and mixes up to 16 decoded voices; it has no source card-type gate or persistent source RAM buffer, and the startup ordering differs. The playback function is a partial host equivalent, not full source initialization parity.

Compared with skaudio.cpp::ALLOC_AUDIO_TABLES at 60-71. Source allocates the loaded-sound shelf, GDAT short-info table, 20 active-sound structures, a zeroed 8-entry sound list, six additional sound structures, and then initializes the RAM playback buffer. Firestaff transfers authenticated sound entries/sample bindings into its bounded queue and has SDL3 16-voice playback, but does not provide the same table set, separate zeroed source sound list, eager audio-buffer initialization or source table ownership. Sound assets and runtime events have partial equivalents; table/startup parity remains open.

Compared with skcore.cpp::ALLOC_NEW_PICT at 1293-1310. SPX v4 allocates CPX heap bytes using rounded 4bpp rows or width bytes for other bpp values, then writes width/height/bpp into the image header and returns the backing buffer. Firestaff's helper computes the payload and header values only; it allocates no pixel buffer, binds no cache index and cannot reproduce source allocation failure or pointer ownership. The picture runtime path remains incomplete.

Compared with skcore.cpp::SOME_RECT_PICT_0b36_0c52 at 1414-1425. Source optionally expands a rectangle, allocates a cache index and an 8bpp picture buffer, resets dirty count, and optionally seeds the initial dirty rectangle. Firestaff records the rectangle/cache-index transition and requested picture allocation, but has no backing picture allocation or live UI cache owner; this route remains partial.

Compared with c_dballocx.cpp::SKW_ALLOC_NEW_PICT at 752-764. DOS allocates CPX memory for width-by-height pixel data, rounds 4bpp row width to an even pixel count, masks total bytes to 16 bits, and writes a pre-buffer header containing bpp, height and width. Firestaff's helper only calculates payload/header values; it does not allocate or return the source-layout buffer and misses the DOS 16-bit total-size wrap. DOS picture-buffer ownership remains open.

Compared with dm2byc.cpp::SKW_0b36_0c52 at 680-689. Compared with xcoreenh.cpp::ADD_PARTY_CHAMPION at 635-644 and its SELECT_CHAMPION_FROM_GDAT helper at 402-427. The source selects a requested GDAT champion, revives it at the current party tile/map, resets resurrection display, assigns party direction/position, sets alive flag 0x4000, then selects slot 0 as leader. The selector itself rejects a held leader-hand object or a full roster, but ADD_PARTY_CHAMPION ignores its return before continuing; its lifecycle also relies on source champion counters, interface redraw, map switching, inventory/tile handling and weight recalculation. Firestaff has bounded source-mirror selection and revive receipts plus leader selection, but no production owner for arbitrary champion addition or the v6 roster/UI mutation. Supported runtime/edition routes remain open.

Compared with dm2D.cpp::driver_keyboardint_T1 at 840-849.
